title: A Survey of Machine Learning Methods for Time Series Prediction
tldr: Comprehensive survey of 79 papers reveals tree-based methods like LightGBM and deep learning methods like LSTM deliver best performance in time series forecasting, with tree-based methods offering significant computational efficiency advantages.
problem_and_motivation: Existing literature reviews struggle to draw meaningful comparisons between models because they analyze independent studies with different implementations and datasets. This heterogeneity prevents direct model comparisons and obscures true performance differences. The survey addresses this gap by reviewing studies that compare both tree-based and deep learning approaches within the same experimental framework.
approach: Conducts systematic survey of 79 influential papers comparing tree-based machine learning and deep learning approaches for time series prediction.
Focuses exclusively on studies with direct comparisons using identical datasets and experimental setups.
Develops two evaluation metrics: First Place Aggregation (FPA) and Weighted Rank Aggregation (WRA) for model comparison.
Analyzes performance across 46 unique time series prediction tasks grouped into 10 categories.
Examines impact of dataset size, time interval, and research focus on model performance.
Evaluates training time efficiency and hyperparameter optimization techniques across studies.
findings: num: Tree-based models outperform deep learning models in 54.55% of tasks studied with FPA metric.
num: LSTM demonstrates strong consistent performance with 58.97% FPA and 0.7222 WRA score across 39 evaluations.
num: Tree-based models are on average 126,934.94% faster than deep learning models in training time.
RNN models excel in environmental, healthcare, and finance-related tasks due to ability to remember long-term dependencies.
Hybrid models generally outperform individual models, with combinations of tree-based and RNN models yielding strong results.
Research focus bias affects observed performance: deep learning-focused papers show DL models outperforming by 33.79% FPA.

key_equations.explanation: First Place Aggregation: frequency with which a model achieves top rank.
Weighted Rank Aggregation: accounts for relative performance across all comparisons.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey contributes a comprehensive analysis of machine learning methods for time series prediction by reviewing 79 papers with direct model comparisons using identical datasets. The work establishes two novel evaluation metrics (FPA and WRA) for systematic model comparison across studies. The survey provides evidence that tree-based methods like LightGBM and deep learning methods like LSTM deliver the best performance, with tree-based methods offering significant computational efficiency advantages. The research offers practical recommendations for approaching time series forecasting tasks based on domain, data characteristics, and computational constraints.
directly_justifies: Tree-based models outperform deep learning models in 54.55% of tasks studied.
LSTM demonstrates strong consistent performance with 58.97% FPA across 39 evaluations.
Tree-based models are on average 126,934.94% faster than deep learning models in training.
Hybrid models generally outperform individual models when combining tree-based and RNN architectures.
Research focus bias affects observed performance outcomes significantly.
limits: Survey limited to papers published between 2017 and 2024 from Web of Science database.
Analysis focuses on comparative studies with identical experimental setups, potentially missing independent evaluations.
Limited representation for some task categories ranging from 3.85% to 21.8% of total papers.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all topic domains identified relevant coverage in domains 6 (predictive modeling) and 12 (evaluation frameworks). Domain 6.A is highly relevant as the survey covers predictive modeling techniques for time series. Domain 6.B is highly relevant as it directly reviews forecasting algorithms for sequential data. Domain 12.A is relevant due to evaluation framework using FPA and WRA metrics. Domains 1-5 (Filipino demographics, cultural practices, expense categorization, existing systems, behavioral profiles) were considered and rejected as not directly relevant. Domains 7-11 (budgeting, anomaly detection, mobile design, privacy, engagement) were considered and rejected as not addressed. Domain 13 (savings/debt management) was considered but rejected as the paper focuses on general time series forecasting rather than personal finance management. Domain 14 (synthetic data and model serving) was considered but rejected as the paper reviews real-world datasets rather than synthetic data generation.
